claim: S3 Replication copies objects automatically and asynchronously across buckets, which can be owned by the same AWS account or by different accounts.
question: Is S3 Replication synchronous or asynchronous?

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 Replication enables automatic, asynchronous copying of objects across Amazon S3 buckets. Buckets that are configured for object replication can be owned by the same AWS account or by different accounts.

claim: Versioning must be enabled on both the source and destination buckets to enable replication.
question: What must be turned on before S3 Replication can be enabled?

values.display: both the source and destination buckets

evidence.quote: Versioning must be enabled for both the source and destination buckets to enable replication.

claim: Replication (CRR and SRR) is configured at the bucket level, a shared prefix level, or the object level using object tags.
question: At what granularity can S3 Replication be configured?

values.display: object level using S3 object tags

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 Replication (CRR and SRR) is configured at the S3 bucket level, a shared prefix level, or an object level using S3 object tags.

claim: CRR gives lower-latency access from other geographic regions and can meet a compliance requirement to keep copies hundreds of miles apart.
question: Why would you use Cross-Region Replication?

evidence.quote: You can use CRR to provide lower-latency data access in different geographic regions. CRR can also help if you have a compliance requirement to store copies of data hundreds of miles apart.

claim: SRR keeps a copy of your data in a separate AWS account in the same Region for data sovereignty and compliance, aggregates logs from several buckets, or mirrors test and development environments.
question: Why would you use Same-Region Replication?

values.display: separate AWS account in the same region

evidence.quote: SRR helps you address data sovereignty and compliance requirements by keeping a copy of your data in a separate AWS account in the same region as the original. You can use SRR to change account ownership for the replicated objects to protect data from accidental deletion. You can also use SRR to easily aggregate logs from different S3 buckets for in-region processing, or to configure live replication between test and development environments.

claim: S3 Batch Replication replicates existing bucket contents, including objects that previously failed to replicate and objects replicated from another source.
question: Can S3 Replication copy objects that existed before the rule was created?

evidence.quote: You can also replicate existing bucket contents (S3 Batch Replication), including existing objects, objects that previously failed to replicate, and objects replicated from another source.
Yes. You can use S3 Batch Replication to replicate existing objects between buckets.

claim: Objects that fail to replicate at first can be re-replicated with S3 Batch Replication.
question: Can failed replication be retried?

values.display: re-replicate objects that fail to replicate initially

evidence.quote: Yes. You can use S3 Batch Replication to re-replicate objects that fail to replicate initially.

claim: Lifecycle actions are not replicated; to apply the same lifecycle to both buckets, enable the same lifecycle configuration on both.
question: Does S3 Replication copy Lifecycle actions to the destination?

evidence.quote: Lifecycle actions are not replicated, and if you want the same lifecycle configuration applied to both source and destination buckets, enable the same lifecycle configuration on both.

claim: Replication rules can write the copies into another storage class, in the same or a different Region.
question: Can replicas land in a different storage class than the source?

evidence.quote: With S3 Replication, you can establish replication rules to make copies of your objects into another storage class, in the same or a different region.

claim: Replication can send data to multiple destination buckets in the same or different Regions, each with its own storage class, encryption and RTC settings.
question: Can one source bucket replicate to several destination buckets?

evidence.quote: Yes. S3 Replication allows customers to replicate their data to multiple destination buckets in the same, or different AWS Regions. When setting up, you simply specify the new destination bucket in your existing replication configuration or create a new replication configuration with multiple destination buckets.

claim: For CRR and SRR you can replicate into a different AWS account and use Ownership Overwrite to give the destination account ownership of the replicated data, keeping source and destination ownership distinct.
question: How does cross-account replication protect against malicious deletion?

evidence.quote: Yes, for CRR and SRR, you can set up replication across AWS accounts to store your replicated data in a different account in the target region. You can use Ownership Overwrite in your replication configuration to maintain a distinct ownership stack between source and destination, and grant destination account ownership to the replicated storage.

claim: Delete markers are replicated only when delete marker replication is enabled in the rule, and it is not supported for tag-based replication rules.
question: Are delete markers replicated?

evidence.quote: Yes, you can replicate delete markers from source to destination if you have delete marker replication enabled in your replication configuration. When you replicate delete markers, Amazon S3 will behave as if the object was deleted in both buckets.
Amazon S3 Replication does not support delete marker replication for object tag based replication rules.

claim: S3 Replication is not available between AWS China Regions and Regions outside China; replication is possible only within the China Regions.
question: Can you replicate between a China Region and another Region?

values.display: not available between AWS China Regions and AWS Regions outside of China

evidence.quote: No, Amazon S3 Replication is not available between AWS China Regions and AWS Regions outside of China. You are only able to replicate within the China regions.

claim: S3 Replication supports all encryption types S3 offers: server-side encryption with SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and SSE-C, and client-side encryption.
question: Which encryption types does S3 Replication support?

evidence.quote: S3 Replication supports all encryption types that S3 offers.

For server-side encryption, S3 offers server-side encryption with Amazon S3-managed keys (SSE-S3), server-side encryption with KMS keys stored in AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS), and server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C).

claim: Replication is billed as destination storage, the primary copy, replication PUT requests and any infrequent-access retrieval charges; CRR also pays inter-Region data transfer out, while SRR has no data transfer charge.
question: What do you pay for S3 Replication, and does SRR have a data transfer charge?

values.display: no data transfer charges for S3 Same Region Replication

evidence.quote: For S3 Replication (Cross-Region Replication and Same Region Replication), you pay the S3 charges for storage in the selected destination S3 storage classes, the storage charges for the primary copy, replication PUT requests, and applicable infrequent access storage retrieval charges. For CRR, you also pay for inter-region Data Transfer OUT From S3 to your destination region.
Data transfer charges only apply for S3 Cross Region Replication (S3 CRR) and S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC), there are no data transfer charges for S3 Same Region Replication (S3 SRR).

claim: In cross-account replication the source account pays for all data transfer and the destination account pays for the replication PUT requests.
question: Who pays for what in cross-account S3 replication?

values.display: destination account pays for the replication PUT requests

evidence.quote: For cross account replication, the source account pays for all data transfer (S3 RTC and S3 CRR) and the destination account pays for the replication PUT requests.

claim: S3 Replication Time Control is designed to replicate most objects in seconds and 99.99% of objects within 15 minutes, backed by an SLA that 99.9% of objects replicate within 15 minutes per Region pair in any billing month.
question: What does S3 Replication Time Control promise?

qualifiers.scope: per replication Region pair, per billing month

evidence.quote: S3 Replication Time Control is designed to replicate most objects in seconds, and 99.99% of objects within 15 minutes. S3 Replication Time Control is backed by a Service Level Agreement (SLA) commitment that 99.9% of objects will be replicated in 15 minutes for each replication region pair during any billing month.

claim: If fewer than 99.9% of objects replicate within 15 minutes for a Region pair in a billing month, the RTC SLA gives a service credit on every object that took longer than 15 minutes.
question: What happens when S3 RTC misses its 15-minute target?

qualifiers.scope: per replication Region pair, per billing month

evidence.quote: If fewer than 99.9% of your objects are replicated in 15 minutes for each replication region pair during a monthly billing cycle, the S3 RTC SLA provides a service credit on any object that takes longer than 15 minutes to replicate.

claim: Replication gives four CloudWatch metrics (operations pending, bytes pending, replication latency, operations failed replication), and s3:Replication event notifications report which objects failed and why.
question: Which replication metrics and failure events exist?

values.display: operations pending, bytes pending, replication latency, and operations failed replication

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 Replication provides four detailed metrics in the Amazon S3 console and in Amazon CloudWatch: operations pending, bytes pending, replication latency, and operations failed replication.
Additionally, you can set up Amazon S3 Event Notifications of s3:Replication type to get more information about objects that failed to replicate and the reason behind the failures.

claim: With RTC enabled you receive an event notification when an object takes more than 15 minutes to replicate, and another when that object then replicates successfully.
question: What events does S3 RTC send about slow replication?

evidence.quote: Finally, if you have S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) enabled you will receive an S3 Event Notification when an object takes more than 15 minutes to replicate, and another when that object replicates successfully to the destination.

claim: Replication metrics and events can be enabled per rule and are enabled by default for rules with Replication Time Control.
question: Are replication metrics on by default?

values.display: enabled by default for S3 Replication Time Control enabled rules

evidence.quote: Amazon S3 Replication metrics and events can be enabled for each new or existing replication rules, and are enabled by default for S3 Replication Time Control enabled rules.

claim: The bytes pending, operations pending and replication latency metrics do not track S3 Batch Replication; use the operations failed replication metric or Batch Operations completion reports instead.
question: Can replication metrics track a Batch Replication job?

values.display: cannot use metrics like bytes pending, operations pending, and replication latency

evidence.quote: You cannot use metrics like bytes pending, operations pending, and replication latency to track S3 Batch Replication progress. However, you can use the operations failed replication metric to monitor existing objects that do not replicate successfully with S3 Batch Replication.

claim: Object tags can be replicated with Cross-Region Replication; configurations enabled earlier need new permissions before tags replicate.
question: Are object tags replicated by CRR?

evidence.quote: Object tags can be replicated across AWS Regions using Cross-Region Replication. For customers with Cross-Region Replication already enabled, new permissions are required in order for tags to replicate.
